title: Azmi and the River That Argued
logline: Azmi fights Jala until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Azmi, who carried determination, resolve, ran headlong against Jala, who was clearness after rain. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Azmi noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Azmi had fought so hard in Jala was only the part of Azmi that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
